label: Skilled bots has no sign-in: identity is owner/name resolved from four sources in precedence order, the installed job's pinned environment variable, the checkout's bots/config.json, the environment, then the git origin remote.
The pinned identity outranks the config because a run with checkout write access could otherwise edit the config to move every lookup under another identity's empty folders.
A pinned value that is not owner/name is refused rather than skipped, so a damaged job never falls back to the checkout.
Identity becomes a filesystem key through encodeURIComponent(identity.toLowerCase()), so every store is already per-identity by construction.
OpenBot has three roles, owner, admin and member: an owner or an admin governs the organization's people, sign-in and policy, and a member uses it.
OpenBot's role list is extensible and forward-compatible, because a client reads a role it does not know as a member.
Only admin and member are assignable in OpenBot; owner is not in AssignableRole, so it is a property of the deployment rather than a grant.
The smallest roles model for a small team is two roles rather than three: the person who owns the machine, implicit because they own the checkout, and everyone else.

Every store is already shared rather than per-person, because identity is the repository and not the person, so everyone running a bot in one checkout resolves the same secret store, connector grants and run folders.
The smallest sign-in is none: the checkout's remote is the identity and a shared host is one Unix user, so a sign-in would put a second identity system beside the one every path already uses.
